zhanggui-verification-before-completion: Proves a completion claim with fresh evidence — real command output, test results, an actual run — before anyone acts on that claim. Use when work is about to be called done, fixed, passing, or ready without fresh evidence for it, including when someone asks for the actual command output rather than a summary, when a commit, push, or handoff is about to rest on that claim, and when the change looks obviously safe.
zhanggui-requesting-code-review: Runs a new independent review of a diff, patch, or set of changed files and reports Critical and Important findings by severity. Use when someone asks for a review, 审查, or 过一遍 of a diff, patch, or changed files, when a change needs a new pair of eyes before it merges or ships, or when only reviewing is wanted with no edit to the code, covering a one-line change, a three-file refactor, and a release script about to go live.
zhanggui-receiving-code-review: Verifies incoming review feedback item by item and gives each one an explicit disposition — accepted, rejected with evidence, or implemented. Use when review feedback, reviewer comments, or a findings report has arrived and each item needs technical verification before it is accepted, rejected, or implemented, even when the feedback sounds obviously right.
zhanggui-using-git-worktrees: Creates an isolated git worktree for feature work so the main working tree stays untouched, and tears one down again when the work is done. Use when feature work needs an isolated checkout, a write scope separated from the main working tree, or a dedicated workspace for executing an implementation plan, and when an existing worktree has to be set up or cleaned up rather than left behind, even if the request never says 'worktree'.
